To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the 18–S rRNA intergenes of higher plants are more similar than previously thought, and a conserved core-like structure exists in these regions.

the 18– 25S intergenic region of tobacco rDNA is 1.5 kb in length, that it contains a 3.0 kb inverted repeat, and that a ‘core’ structure can be identified which contains the processed sites in a similar arrangement to other organisms.
the rDNA intergenic regions in higher plants have conserved secondary structure, and that this secondary structure is maintained despite extensive sequence variation in the rDNA intergene region.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of conserved and function-specific features within rRNA intergenic regions.
the identification of conserved and function-specific regions within the intergenic region of the 18S–25S ribosomal DNA.
the structure of the rDNA intergenic region in higher plants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is an extensive conservation of structure in the intergenic region of the rRNA gene cluster of higher plants.

the 18–19S rRNA intergenics of higher plants contain a core-like structure which is highly conserved, a 5′ region which contains the 18S rRNA processing site and is highly conserved and a 3′ region which contains both the 25S rRNA processing and transcriptional initiation sites and is highly divergent.
the 18–S rRNA intergenes in the higher plants are highly conserved in sequence, structure and function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 18–S rRNA intergenes are more conserved than previously recognized, and that the conserved regions are not confined to the highly conserved regions.

the 18–S rRNA intergenes in the rDNA of higher plants have been highly conserved in sequence, structure and function, and that this conservation is reflected in the conservation of the 18S–5.8S rRNA processed sites.
the rDNA intergenic regions of the higher plants are highly homologous, and that this homology is due to the retention of a core structure which maintains the processed site in close proximity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 3’ end of the 18S rRNA and the 5’ end of the large subunit are in close proximity in a region of conserved secondary structure.
, in spite of the large number of sequence differences, there is a conserved structure in the 25–18S spacer region of higher plant rDNA which is maintained in all of the sequences.
the 3′ end of the 18S rRNA gene and the 5′ end of the ITS1 region of rDNA are highly conserved and may be involved in a common function.
